video_title: Stephen A. addresses the REALITY of Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers' situation | First Take

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith criticizes Steve Ballmer's management of the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: Steve Ballmer, he needs to stop.
quotes.quote: Steve Ballmer, he needs to stop. The reality of the situation is that there is a preponderance of evidence for different companies endorsed a man that never showed up for anything to endorse. He never did anything. Kawhi Leonard, he's missed 40% of his regular season games, 30% of his playoff games. Steve Ballmer has paid him $291 million since he arrived as a Clipper.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith calls out Dennis Robertson for his role in Kawhi Leonard's situation
quotes.excerpt: Dennis Robertson, his uncle, that's been negotiating on his behalf for all of these years.
quotes.quote: Dennis Robertson, his uncle, that's been negotiating on his behalf for all of these years, who has a history of asking for stuff that far exceeds the parameters and the lines of rules and regulations governing the NBA and its collective bargaining agreement. This man has been at it for years in San Antonio, in Toronto, when he's communicated with the Lakers and various other teams. Kawhi Leonard unleashed him out to the world on Kawhi Leonard's behalf for over a decade.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler discusses the likelihood of the Clippers trade happening
quotes.excerpt: this trade is likely going to happen.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: It's not going to be Kawhi Leonard because this trade, Shams Charania reported already this morning, this trade is likely going to happen and they're going to immediately get two first-round picks back. I don't think the Clippers got hit as hard here as they could. If they're allowed to make this trade, this contract could have been voided.

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: But it's not going to be Kawhi Leonard because they're right.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler criticizes Kawhi Leonard's statement regarding his inner circle
quotes.excerpt: Kawhi Leonard's statement yesterday is repugnant on an incredible level and it should go into the Hall of Fame.
quotes.quote: Kawhi Leonard's statement yesterday is repugnant on an incredible level and it should go into the Hall of Fame of statements because he starts this statement off, Stephen A., with the following sentence: 'Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am.' That is a preposterous sentence. And then it's outdone by the second sentence: 'I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle.' He blames other people in his inner circle, pays a paltry fine based on the money that he was illicitly given, announces that he's got a clean slate.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen A. Smith argues Adam Silver should have been harsher on Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: Adam Silver does have the power to look at Kawhi Leonard's statement and modify his position.
quotes.quote: Adam Silver does have the power to look at Kawhi Leonard's statement and dare I say modify his position. I would, based on that statement from Kawhi Leonard alone, I would null and void the trade. You ain't going to Toronto, your ass going to stay right there in LA, and you going to suffer the consequences with this team.

quotes.speaker: Ramona Shelburne
quotes.summary_phrase: Ramona Shelburne explains why the NBA didn't void Kawhi Leonard's contract
quotes.excerpt: if that investigation showed any proof of Kawhi Leonard having knowledge, that voiding of a contract
quotes.quote: There won't be any change in the NBA's ruling with Kawhi Leonard. They had full awareness of what that statement was going to be. But if that investigation showed any proof of Kawhi Leonard having knowledge, that voiding of a contract, that was certainly on the table. But the investigation didn't show that. There was a clear power dynamic issue between him and his uncle Dennis Robertson. Uncle Dennis Robertson was widely known around the NBA for having just out of control, preposterous asks.
